     (III) Directors and the Board

         During the Reporting Period, the Company completed the re-election of members of the Board.
         The Board of the Company currently comprises 9 Directors, including 5 non-independent Directors,
         3 independent Directors, and 1 employee Director. Based on the original four regular specialized
         committees, the Company optimized and adjusted its committee structure by newly establishing the
         Sustainability Committee, forming a structure of five major specialized committees, including the Strategy
         Committee, Sustainability Committee, Nomination Committee, Audit Committee, and Remuneration
         and Appraisal Committee. The Company continuously strengthened the Board’s development, strictly
         implemented its authorities, promoted standardized operations, and continuously enhanced the
         efficiency and professionalism of decision-making. This ensured effective fulfillment of the Board’s core
         responsibilities of formatting strategy, making decisions, and preventing risks. All Directors adhered to
         principles of integrity, diligence, and responsibility, leveraging their professional expertise and capabilities
         to make independent, objective, and impartial judgments on proposals reviewed by the Board, exercising
         their rights and fulfilling their obligations in accordance with the law.


         Independent Directors fully utilized their expert advantages and supportive role in decision-making,
         providing crucial safeguard for the professional and scientific decision-making of the Board. During
         the Reporting Period, the Company held a total of 12 Board meetings. Each specialized committee
         performed its duties with precision and synergy. the Strategy Committee focused on the Company’s
         long-term development planning, and held four meetings; the Sustainability Committee focused on the
         Company’s ESG governance, green and low-carbon initiatives, and social responsibility efforts, and
         held 1 meeting; the Audit Committee strengthened oversight and scrutiny, convening 9 meetings; the
         Nomination Committee and the Remuneration and Appraisal Committee, centered on talent development
         and incentive mechanisms improvement, collectively held 6 meetings, thereby providing professional
         support for the Board’s scientific decision-making.

     (IV) Information Disclosure and Transparency

         The Company’s Board regards information disclosure as a core mechanism for fulfilling governance
         responsibilities and maintaining capital market order, as well as a critical bridge for building trust with
         the Company, investors and the public. Adhering strictly to the core principles of “truthfulness, accuracy,
         completeness, timeliness, and fairness”, the Board consistently focuses on enhancing the quality of
         information disclosure and strengthening market communication transparency. It continuously optimizes
         the information disclosure management system, proactively improves voluntary information disclosure
         practices, and effectively safeguards investors’ rights to information, participation, and oversight.
         During the Reporting Period, the Company completed the preparation and disclosure of 152 A Shares
         compliance documents including regular reports, temporary announcements and other disclosure
         documents, and completed the disclosure of 143 various types of H Shares documents. Through
         standardized and transparent governance efficacy, the Company has solidified its foundation of trust in
         the capital market. The Company continued to refine its supporting systems for information disclosure,
         constantly improved internal reporting and review mechanisms, strengthened full-process control over
         information disclosure, and strictly implemented relevant regulations on inside information management to
         effectively mitigate various compliance risks. Guided by investor needs, the Company strove to improve
         the readability and accessibility of periodic reports, and continuously expanded the breadth and depth of
         operational disclosures to more clearly present its business development. With its standardized, efficient,
         high-quality, and transparent information disclosure practices, the Company was evaluated and awarded
         grade A for its information disclosure on the Shanghai Stock Exchange for the year 2024-2025 for eight
         consecutive years. This achievement reflects strong recognition from regulators and the capital market.

 (VI) Shareholders’ Rights

     Shareholder(s) severally or jointly holding 10% or above of the Shares of the Company who request
     the Board to convene an extraordinary general meeting shall put forward such request to the Board in
     writing. The Board shall, pursuant to laws, administrative regulations and the Articles of Association,
     give a written reply on whether or not to convene the extraordinary general meeting within 10 days after
     receipt of the request. If the Board agrees to convene the extraordinary general meeting, it shall serve a
     notice of the shareholders’ meeting within five days after the resolution is made by the Board, and the
     consent of the relevant Shareholder(s) shall be obtained in the event of any change to the original request
     set forth in the notice. If the Board does not agree to convene the extraordinary general meeting, or
     fails to give a reply within 10 days after receipt of the request, Shareholder(s) severally or jointly holding
     10% or above of the Shares of the Company may propose to the Audit Committee the convening of
     an extraordinary general meeting, and shall put forward such request to the Audit Committee in writing.
     If the Audit Committee agrees to convene the extraordinary general meeting, it shall serve a notice of
     the shareholders’ meeting within five days after receipt of the request, and the consent of the relevant
     Shareholder(s) shall be obtained in the event of any change to the original request set forth in the notice.
     If the Audit Committee fails to issue the notice of the shareholders’ meeting within the prescribed period,
     it shall be deemed that the Audit Committee has not convened or presided over the shareholders’
     meeting, and Shareholder(s) severally or jointly holding 10% or above of the Shares of the Company for
     90 consecutive days or more may convene and preside over the shareholders’ meeting on their own.
78   SHANDONG GOLD MINING CO., LTD.

         The convener will give notice to all Shareholders by way of announcement 20 days before the date
         of the annual general meeting, and 15 days before the date of the extraordinary general meeting. The
         notice of a shareholders’ meeting shall include the following: (1) the time, place and duration of the
         meeting; (2) the matters and proposals to be considered at the meeting; (3) a clear statement that all
         ordinary Shareholders, holders of Shares with special voting rights and other Shareholders are entitled
         to attend the shareholders’ meeting and may, in writing, appoint proxies to attend the meeting and vote
         on their behalf, and that such proxies need not be Shareholders of the Company; (4) the record date for
         Shareholders entitled to attend the shareholders’ meeting; (5) the name and telephone number of the
         standing contact person for meeting affairs; and (6) the time and procedures for voting by way of internet
         or other means. The notice of the shareholders’ meeting and any supplementary notice shall fully and
         completely disclose all the specific contents of all proposals.


         When the Company convenes a shareholders’ meeting, the Board, the Audit Committee, and
         Shareholders severally or jointly holding 1% or above of the Shares of the Company are entitled to
         put forward proposals to the Company. Shareholder(s) severally or jointly holding 1% or above of the
         Shares of the Company may submit written provisional proposals to the convener 10 days before a
         shareholders’ meeting is convened.


         Voting at a shareholders’ meeting is conducted by way of poll.


         The Group communicates with Shareholders through the publication of annual reports, interim reports,
         quarterly reports, press and electronic announcements. All communications with Shareholders are also
         published on the Group’s website (http://www.sdhjgf.com.cn).

 The Company is completely independent from its controlling Shareholder in terms of assets, business,
 organization, finance and personnel. The Company possesses an independent and complete business system
 and independent operation capabilities. The Company is not aware of any non-operational appropriation
 of the Company’s capital and assets by the controlling Shareholder. There is no business reliance on the
 controlling Shareholder, the de facto controller, or other related parties.


 (I)    Assets: The Company’s assets are independent and complete, with clear ownership rights. The
        Company manages its assets independently, and the property rights relationship between the Company
        and its controlling Shareholder is explicit and clear.


 (II)   Personnel: The Company possesses an independent and comprehensive personnel management
        system with corresponding rules and regulations. The Company independently signs labor contracts with
        employees, and its personnel, salary and remuneration, and social security matters are managed entirely
        independently.


 (III) Finance: The Company has an independent finance department and financial staff, with an independent
       accounting system and financial management framework, making financial decisions independently. It
        maintains independent bank accounts, conducts investment and financing activities in accordance with
        regulations, and files taxes separately as required by law. There is no intervention by the controlling
        Shareholder in the Company’s use of funds.


 (IV) Organization: The Company has an independent and sound corporate governance structure. In line
      with the regulatory requirements for listed companies and the Company’s actual business needs, it has
      established a robust organizational framework that is entirely separate from the controlling Shareholder.
      The setup procedures and functions of the organization are independent.


 (V)    Business: The Company has an independent and complete business system, conducts its business
        operations autonomously, and is entirely separate from the controlling Shareholder. Any transactions with
        the de facto controller, controlling Shareholder, or related parties are conducted in strict compliance with
        regulatory rules to perform review and information disclosure procedures, with no instances detrimental
        to the Company’s interests, particularly those of minority Shareholders.

      (VIII) Primary Duties of the Specialized Committees

          1.   Nomination Committee

               The primary duties of the Nomination Committee include:


               (1)   to make recommendations to the Board on the size and composition of the Board according
                     to the operating activities, size of assets and shareholding structure of the Company; to review
                     the structure, size, composition and relevant qualifications (including skills, expertise and
                     experience) of the Board at least once annually, make recommendations on any adjustment
                     to the Board pursuant to the development strategy of the Company, and formulate a diversity
                     policy for the Board;


               (2)   to study the selection criteria, procedures and methods of Directors and managers and make
                     recommendations in this regard to the Board;


               (3)   to identify competent candidates for Directors and managers extensively;


               (4)   to make recommendations to the Board on the candidates for Directors and managers,
                     and provide advice to the Board on the appointment or re-appointment of Directors and
                     the succession plan for Directors (in particular the chairman of the Board and the general
                     manager);
                                                                                   Annual Report 2025   105


SECTION 4 CORPORATE GOVERNANCE, ENVIRONMENT AND SOCIETY

      (5)   to screen the candidates for other management members and provide advice to the Board; to
            conduct a review and make recommendations on other senior management members who are
            subject to appointment by the Board;


      (6)   to evaluate the overall skills, knowledge and experience of Directors and senior management,
            and to assess the independence of the independent non-executive Directors; and


      (7)   all other matters delegated by the Board.


      Procedure and Basis for Nomination


      The Nomination Committee shall, in accordance with the relevant laws and regulations and the
      Articles of Association, and having regard to the actual circumstances of the Company, formulate
      the selection requirements, procedures and term of office of Directors and management of the
      Company, formulate resolutions and submit such resolutions to the Board for approval and
      implementation. It is stipulated in the implementation rules that the Nomination Committee shall hold
      at least two meetings each year.


      The selection process of Directors and managers is as follows:


      (1)   The Nomination Committee should actively communicate with the relevant departments and
            study the Company’s demand for Directors and managers, and present such information in
            writing;


      (2)   The Nomination Committee may search extensively for candidates for Directors and managers
            from within the Company, its holding (associate) enterprises and the market;


      (3)   Gather information about the occupation, academic qualifications, post titles, detailed work
            experience and all the concurrent posts of the candidates, and present such information in
            writing;


      (4)   Seek the nominees’ consent for nomination; otherwise, the nominees cannot be the candidates
            for Directors or managers;


      (5)   Convene a Nomination Committee meeting to review the qualifications of the candidates
            against the criteria for Directors and managers;


      (6)   Make recommendations to the Board regarding the candidates for Directors and the candidates
            for new managers, together with the relevant materials, one to two months before the election
            of new Directors and the appointment of new managers; and


      (7)   Complete other follow-up work according to the decisions and feedback of the Board.
106   SHANDONG GOLD MINING CO., LTD.


 SECTION 4 CORPORATE GOVERNANCE, ENVIRONMENT AND SOCIETY

          2.   Remuneration and Appraisal Committee

               The primary duties and authorities of the Remuneration and Appraisal Committee are as follows:


               (1)   to make recommendations to the Board on remuneration plans or proposals and the
                     establishment of formal and transparent procedures for the formulation of the above
                     remuneration plans or proposals, according to the primary scope, responsibilities and
                     importance of the management positions of Directors and senior management members and
                     the remuneration standards of relevant positions in other relevant enterprises;


               (2)   the remuneration plans or proposals shall include, but not be limited to, performance appraisal
                     criteria, procedures and key appraisal system, and major incentive and penalty plans and
                     systems;


               (3)   to determine the specific remuneration packages of all executive Directors and senior
                     management, including benefits in kind, pension rights and compensation payments (including
                     any compensation payable for loss or termination of office or appointment), and to make
                     recommendations to the Board on the remuneration of non-executive Directors;


               (4)   to review and approve the performance-based remuneration packages by making reference to
                     the corporate objectives approved from time to time by the Board;


               (5)   to review the performance of duties of the Directors (non-independent Directors) and the senior
                     management of the Company, and to conduct annual performance appraisals on them;


               (6)   to examine and approve compensation payable to executive Directors and senior management
                     for any loss or termination of office or appointment, to ensure that such compensation is
                     determined in accordance with the relevant contractual terms; or, where not so determined,
                     that such compensation is fair and reasonable and does not impose an undue burden on the
                     Company;


               (7)   to review and approve compensation arrangements relating to the dismissal or removal of
                     Directors for misconduct, to ensure that such arrangements are determined in accordance
                     with the relevant contractual terms; or, where not so determined, that such compensation is
                     reasonable and appropriate; to ensure that no Director or any of his/her associates (as defined
                     in the Hong Kong Listing Rules) is involved in deciding his/her own remuneration;


               (8)   to supervise the implementation of the Company’s remuneration system;


               (9)   to review and/or approve matters relating to share schemes under Chapter 17 of the Hong
                     Kong Listing Rules; and


               (10) to perform other duties as conferred by laws and regulations, the relevant regulatory rules
                     of the place where the Company is listed (such as the Hong Kong Listing Rules), rules of
                     procedure and the Board.

    3.   Audit Committee

         The primary duties of the Audit Committee include:


         (1)   to make recommendations to the Board regarding the appointment, re-appointment or
               dismissal of external auditors; to provide recommendations to the Board, and to approve the
               remuneration and terms of engagement of the external auditors; and to deal with all matters
               relating to the resignation or dismissal of external auditors;


         (2)   to review and monitor the independence and objectivity of the external auditors and the
               effectiveness of the audit process in accordance with applicable standards;


         (3)   to formulate and implement policies relating to the engagement of external auditors for non-
               audit services;


         (4)   to supervise the internal audit system of the Company and its implementation; to examine
               the truthfulness, completeness and accuracy of the financial statements, annual reports
               and accounts, half-year reports and quarterly reports (if any) of the Company, and to review
               important opinions regarding financial reporting in such statements and reports;


         (5)   to review the financial information and its disclosure of the Company;


         (6)   to review the financial control, internal control and risk management systems of the Company,
               and to audit material connected transactions;


         (7)   to discuss with the management on risk management and internal control systems to ensure
               that the management has performed its duty to maintain effective risk management and internal
               control systems;


         (8)   to review the major findings of investigations on risk management and internal control, and the
               management’s response to such findings on its own initiative or as delegated by the Board;
               and


         (9)   to review the financial and accounting policies and practices of the Group.

      (II) Remuneration Policies

           √ Applicable   □ N/A


           Guided by its strategy and the principle of market-oriented distribution, the Company has established a
           position-based performance salary system that is internally competitive, equitable and motivating, while
           remaining externally competitive in the market. The Company implements company-wide performance
           appraisal and reinforces the incentive role of performance. For senior management, the Company signs
           annual target responsibility statements, determines annual remuneration standards with reference to
           market levels, and pays out performance-based compensation based on the assessment results against
           the targets set in the statements.


      (III) Training Plan

           √ Applicable   □ N/A


           In 2025, the Company continuously strengthened exchanges and cooperation with external institutions
           in employee training, launching initiatives such as the “Bringing Training to Enterprises” program to
           effectively enhance the comprehensive capabilities of its workforce.


           Management Personnel Training: In collaboration with renowned domestic and international research
           institutions, the Company conducted training programs for management personnel at various levels.
           The training covered multiple areas including production operations, human resources, engineering
           management, financial auditing, financial management, and resource mergers and acquisitions.


           Professional and Technical Personnel Training: A continuing education system for professional and
           technical personnel was established, covering 13 specialties including geology, surveying, mining, mineral
           processing, electromechanical, and others. Additionally, a learning system for the Expert Committee
           was implemented, covering 5 specialties including geology, surveying, mining, mineral processing,
           and electromechanical. These initiatives have effectively enhanced the professional competence of the
           Company’s technical staff.

VIII. PROPOSAL ON PROFIT DISTRIBUTION OR TRANSFER OF CAPITAL
      RESERVE

  (I)   Formulation and Implementation of or Adjustment to the Cash Dividend Policy

        √ Applicable   □ N/A


        1.   Formulation of profit distribution policy
             In order to effectively protect the legitimate rights and interests of small and medium Shareholders,
             establish and improve shareholder return mechanisms, enhance the transparency and operability
             of the profit distribution policy decision-making process, and proactively reward investors, the
             Company, in accordance with the Opinions of the General Office of the State Council on Further
             Strengthening the Protection of Legitimate Rights and Interests of Small and Medium Investors
             in Capital Markets (Guo Ban Fa [2013] No. 110) and the “No. 3 Guidance for Listed Companies
             Supervision — Cash Dividends of Listed Companies”, and other laws, regulations and normative
             documents, considered and approved the “Proposal on Formulating ‘The Company’s Shareholder
             Return Plan for the Next Three Years (2023-2025)’” at the 35th meeting of the Sixth Session of
             the Board of Directors and the 19th meeting of the Sixth Session of the Supervisory Committee
             held on 24 February 2023, and at the Second Extraordinary General Meeting of 2023 and the First
             A Share and H Share Class General Meetings of 2023 held on 23 March 2023; furthermore, at
             the 74th meeting of the Sixth Session of the Board of Directors and the 46th meeting of the Sixth
             Session of the Supervisory Committee held on 28 July 2025 and the Third Extraordinary General
             Meeting of 2025 held on 14 August 2025, the Company considered and approved the “Resolution
             regarding the Abolition of Supervisory Committee, Amendments to the ‘Articles of Association’
             and the Completion of Registration and Filing”, making corresponding revisions to the Company’s
             profit distribution policy, thereby further improving the forms, decision-making mechanisms, and
             procedures for profit distribution. The main contents are as follows:


             The Company’s profit distribution policies are as follows:


             (I)   Principle of Profit Distribution: The Company shall adhere to a principle of sustained and
                   stable profit distribution. The distribution of profits shall emphasize providing shareholders with
                   reasonable returns on their investments while taking into account the long-term interests of the
                   Company, the interests of all Shareholders and the sustainable development of the Company.
112   SHANDONG GOLD MINING CO., LTD.


 SECTION 4 CORPORATE GOVERNANCE, ENVIRONMENT AND SOCIETY

              (II)   Form of Profit Distribution: The Company may distribute profits in the form of cash, shares,
                     or a combination of cash and shares. When the conditions for cash dividends are met, cash
                     dividends are preferred shares dividends. The Company’s cash dividend policy goal is the
                     residual dividend policy.


              (III) Profit distribution period: The Company generally distributes profits on an annual basis and
                    may also distribute interim profits (in cash) based on its capital requirements.


              (IV) Differentiated cash dividend policy: When actually distributing dividends, the Company’s Board
                   of Directors shall comprehensively consider factors such as the characteristics of the industry
                   in which the Company operates, its stage of development, its business model, its profitability
                   level, and whether there are significant capital expenditure arrangements. Based on these
                   considerations, the Board shall differentiate among the following situations and propose a
                   differentiated cash dividend policy:


                     1.   When the Company is in a mature stage of development and has no significant capital
                          expenditure arrangements, the proportion of cash dividends distributed in the current
                          profit distribution shall be no less than 80%;


                     2.   When the Company is in a mature stage of development and has significant capital
                          expenditure arrangements, the proportion of cash dividends distributed in the current
                          profit distribution shall be no less than 40%;


                     3.   When the Company is in a growth stage of development and has significant capital
                          expenditure arrangements, the proportion of cash dividends distributed in the current
                          profit distribution shall be no less than 20%;


                          If the Company’s stage of development is difficult to determine but it has significant capital
                          expenditure arrangements, the provisions of the preceding paragraph may apply.


                          The proportion of cash dividends in the current profit distribution shall be calculated as
                          cash dividends divided by the sum of cash dividends and stock dividends.


                          When conditions for cash dividends are met, the Company’s Board of Directors may
                          propose an interim cash distribution based on the Company’s profitability and capital
                          requirements.


              (V)    Interval and Proportion of Cash Dividends: The Company shall have at least one cash
                     dividend distribution every three consecutive years. The specific distribution proportion shall
                     be determined by the Board of Directors based on the Company’s operating conditions and
                     the relevant provisions of the CSRC, and shall be reviewed and approved by the shareholders’
                     meeting.


                     The cumulative profits distributed by the Company in cash over the most recent three years
                     shall be no less than 30% of the average annual distributable profits realized over the same
                     three-year period.
                                                                                       Annual Report 2025   113


SECTION 4 CORPORATE GOVERNANCE, ENVIRONMENT AND SOCIETY

      (VI) The Company may not distribute profits under the following circumstances:


             1.   The audit report of the latest year is an unqualified opinion or an unqualified opinion with
                  significant uncertainties related to going concern;


             2.   The net operating cash flow of the distribution year is negative;


             3.   There are major investment plans or significant cash expenditures (except for fund
                  raising projects). Significant investment plans or significant cash expenditures refer to
                  the proposed external investment, acquisition of assets or purchase of equipment by
                  the Company in the coming twelve months with accumulated expenses amounting to or
                  exceeding 50% of the latest audited net assets of the Company.


             4.   The Company’s asset-liability ratio is higher than 70%.


      (VII) Conditions for Share Dividend Distribution. Subject to the conditions for cash dividend
            distribution being met, if the Company’s operating revenue and net profit are growing rapidly,
            and the Board of Directors considers the Company’s share capital size and equity structure
            reasonable, the Board may, in addition to proposing a cash dividend distribution plan, propose
            and implement a share dividend distribution plan.


      Procedures for decision-making on profit distribution by the Company:


      (I)    The Board of Directors of the Company is responsible for formulating the profit distribution
             plan. In the process of formulating the profit distribution plan, the Board of Directors should
             fully discuss with the independent Directors and the Audit Committee, listen to the opinions of
             public shareholders through multiple channels and ways, and demonstrate the rationality of the
             profit distribution plan; and carefully study and discuss, among others, the timing, conditions as
             well as the minimum ratio, conditions for adjustments and the requirements of the procedures
             for decision-making in respect of the cash dividend distribution of the Company.


      (II)   Before the shareholders’ meeting considers the specific cash dividend proposal, the Company
             actively communicates with shareholders, especially minority shareholders, through various
             means, fully listens to the opinions and demands of minority shareholders, and timely answers
             to the concerns of minority shareholders.


      (III) Independent Directors have the right to express independent opinions if they think that the
            specific cash dividend proposal may harm the rights and interests of the Company or minority
            shareholders. If the opinions of the independent Directors are not adopted or fully adopted by
            the Board of Directors, the opinions of the independent Directors and the specific reasons for
            non-adoption shall be recorded in the resolution of the Board of Directors and disclosed.
114   SHANDONG GOLD MINING CO., LTD.


 SECTION 4 CORPORATE GOVERNANCE, ENVIRONMENT AND SOCIETY

               The consideration procedures of the profit distribution proposal mainly include:


               (I)    Consideration and approval by the Audit Committee according to the procedures;


               (II)   Consideration and approval by the Board of Directors;


               (III) The shareholders’ meeting shall consider and approve it by ordinary resolutions. When the
                     shareholders’ meeting of the Company discusses and considers profit distribution matters, it
                     can adopt various methods such as online voting and setting up an investor communication
                     platform on the Company’s website as needed to provide opportunities for public shareholders
                     to express their opinions and demands.

               Shanghai Securities News, Securities Times, and Securities Daily on 17 July 2025 and 16 October

               The 2024 annual cash dividends for the Company’s A Shares and H Shares were fully distributed
               on 24 July 2025 and 11 August 2025, respectively; the 2025 semi-annual cash dividends were fully
               distributed on 23 October 2025 and 27 October 2025, respectively.

          3.   Adjustments or changes to the Company’s profit distribution policy during the
               Reporting Period

 X. CONSTRUCTION AND IMPLEMENTATION OF INTERNAL CONTROL
    SYSTEM DURING THE REPORTING PERIOD

      √ Applicable   □ N/A


      The Company strictly complies with laws and regulations such as the Company Law and the Code of
      Corporate Governance for Listed Companies, as well as the relevant regulatory requirements and rules of
      the Shanghai Stock Exchange and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. In accordance with the Basic Standards
      for Enterprise Internal Control and its supporting guidelines, the Company has conducted a comprehensive
      review, revision, and update of its existing internal control system to ensure that the system remains
      consistent with the latest regulatory requirements. Focusing on key business processes including production
      and operations, investments and financing, and financial management, the Company has completed
      optimization designs and strengthened risk control points at each stage, further consolidating its internal
      control management foundation.


      The Company consistently prioritizes the self-assessment of its internal controls, having established
      and implemented a self-assessment working mechanism characterized by unified deployment and
      graded implementation. During the evaluation process, the Company strictly adheres to the principles
      of comprehensiveness, materiality, objectivity, and risk-orientation, conducting a holistic and systematic
      assessment of internal control elements, including the internal environment, risk assessment, control activities,
      information and communication, and internal supervision. Through in-depth analysis of the rationality of the
      internal control system’s design and the effectiveness of its operation, the Company promptly identifies and
      rectifies any weak links within the system, effectively preventing various operational and management risks.


      For the year, the Company has achieved significant results in the construction and implementation of its
      internal control system, with continued improvement in the standardization and effectiveness of its internal
      control management. The building of the Company’s internal control system is a long-term and systematic
      endeavor requiring continuous improvement and optimization. In the future, the Company will continuously
      enhance its internal control management level and effectively prevent various risks by promoting the deep
      integration of internal control management with corporate governance, comprehensively deepening risk
      management capabilities, accelerating the digitalization of internal controls, fostering a company-wide culture
      of internal control compliance, continuously optimizing business processes, and strengthening internal and
      external collaboration. These efforts aim to provide a solid guarantee for the Company’s achievement of
      sustainable, high-quality development.


      The Company’s 2025 Internal Control Evaluation Report has been reviewed and approved at the 9th Meeting
      of the Seventh Session of the Board of Directors. For details, please refer to the disclosure on the Shanghai
      Stock Exchange website (http://www.sse.com.cn).

XI. M A N A G E M E N T A N D C O N T R O L O F S U B S I D I A R I E S D U R I N G T H E
    REPORTING PERIOD

   √ Applicable   □ N/A


   During the Reporting Period, the Company continuously deepened its management and control system over
   subsidiaries. By optimizing governance structures, strengthening risk prevention and control, and enhancing
   operational efficiency, the Company ensured overall strategic synergy and compliant, stable operations.


   1.   Improving Governance Structures and Strengthening the Institutionalized Management
        System

        Adhering to the principles of “unified strategy, clear rights and responsibilities, and controllable risks”, the
        Company continuously improved the corporate governance structures of its subsidiaries. By dynamically
        revising the lists of rights and responsibilities, optimizing the rules of procedure for the Board of
        Directors, and clarifying decision-making boundaries at each level, governance efficiency was enhanced.
        Simultaneously, the Company further streamlined its management chains and improved decision-making
        efficiency by reducing legal entity tiers and integrating overseas management platforms.


   2.   Perfecting Corporate Governance Mechanisms and Deepening the Construction of
        the Board of Directors

        Each subsidiary strictly complied with relevant requirements of the Company Law, the Code of Corporate
        Governance for Listed Companies, and other regulations, strengthening the construction of their boards
        of directors and actively leveraging the board’s role in “setting strategy, making decisions, and preventing
        risks”. The parent company exercised management and control over its subsidiaries by appointing or
        nominating directors to the subsidiaries, as well as nominating or recommending senior management
        personnel such as general managers, deputy general managers, and chief financial officers for the
        subsidiaries.


   3.   Strengthening Institutional Alignment and Enforcement Supervision

        The Company promoted the deep integration of internal control with business operations. By sorting
        out business processes, identifying key risk points, and setting control nodes, it achieved full-process
        institutional coverage and enforcement supervision. A comprehensive, end-to-end risk control system
        was established, strengthening the routine monitoring of safety, environmental, and compliance risks,
        improving risk warning and response efficiency, and preventing systemic risks.

         Kong Listing Rules in relation to the appointment of at least three independent non-executive Directors,

      (II) Chairman and General Manager

          The chairman and general manager of the Company are two clearly distinct positions, and their
          respective responsibilities are clearly set out in the Articles of Association. The primary duties of the
          chairman are: to preside over shareholders’ meetings and to convene and preside over Board meetings;
          to urge and inspect the implementation of Board resolutions; to sign Share certificates of the Company;
          to sign important documents of the Board and other documents; in the event of an emergency such
          as a major natural disaster or other force majeure, to exercise special powers of disposal over the
          affairs of the Company that are consistent with the relevant laws and regulations and the interests of
          the Company, and to report to the Board and the shareholders’ meeting thereafter; and to exercise
          such other authorities as may be conferred by the Board. The primary duties of the general manager
          are: to preside over the production and operation management of the Company; to organise the
          implementation of Board resolutions and report to the Board; to organise the implementation of the
          Company’s annual operation plans and investment plans; to formulate proposals for the establishment
          of internal management departments of the Company; to formulate the basic management systems of
          the Company; to formulate specific rules and regulations of the Company; to propose to the Board the
          appointment or dismissal of any vice general manager and the chief financial officer of the Company; to
          decide on the appointment or dismissal of management personnel other than those to be appointed or
          dismissed by the Board; and to exercise such other authorities as may be conferred by the Articles of
          Association or the Board.


          The chairman of the Company is mainly responsible for overall and strategic development, investment
          planning and human resources allocation, and has delegated the day-to-day operational management to
          relevant management personnel. The executive Directors and the vice general managers of the Group
          are responsible for the day-to-day management of various matters (including the implementation of
          Board resolutions), and report to the general manager on the business operations of the Group.

      (III) Meeting Practices and Conduct

          Board meetings include regular Board meetings and extraordinary Board meetings. Regular Board
          meetings shall be held at least four times a year, and shall be convened by the chairman, with written
          notice to be given to all Directors and Supervisors at least 14 days before the date of the meeting.
          Regular Board meetings shall not be convened by way of correspondence.


          An extraordinary Board meeting may be held by request of Shareholders representing more than 1/10 of
          the voting rights, more than 1/3 of Directors, or the Audit Committee. The chairman shall convene and
          preside over a Board meeting within 10 days after receipt of the proposal. Notice of an extraordinary
          Board meeting shall be given by telephone or in writing, and the time limit for the delivery of such notice
          shall be at least three days before the meeting. In urgent circumstances where an extraordinary Board
          meeting is required to be held as soon as possible, notice of the meeting may be given at any time by
          telephone or orally, in which case the convener shall give an explanation at the meeting.


          The Board shall keep minutes of resolutions passed at meetings of the Board. Directors present at a
          meeting shall sign the minutes. Minutes of the Board meetings shall be kept as records of the Company
          for a period of 10 years.


          If any Director has a connected relationship with the enterprise involved in any resolution made at a
          Board meeting, the said Director shall not exercise voting rights on such resolution himself or on behalf
          of any other Director.

   (II) Philosophies of the Company

         The development concept of the Company is “Safe Shandong Gold, Ecological Shandong Gold, Vibrant
         Shandong Gold and Humanistic Shandong Gold”. The enterprise spirit of the Company is the pursuit of
         excellence and pioneering innovation. The brand image of the Company is “Shandong Gold, Ecological
         Mining”. The core values of the Company are openness, inclusiveness, loyalty and responsibility.
         The tenet of the Company is benefiting employees, repaying Shareholders, benefiting society and
         contributing to a powerful country. The cooperation philosophy of the Company is respect, integration,
         mutual benefit and sharing. The management philosophy of the Company is resource focused, benefit
         first and innovation centered. The safety and environmental protection philosophy of the Company is
         “Zero accident in both safety and environmental protection”. The talent philosophy of the Company is
         to select capable and high-caliber talents with both moral integrity and professional competence. The
         Party building philosophy of the Company is sticking to the revolutionary heritage and keeping in mind
         the original aspiration and missions. The integrity philosophy of the Company is upholding integrity and
         frugality, and maintaining a clean and upright atmosphere. The care philosophy of the Company is the “Three
         Yeses” and “Three Nos” commitment.

      (IV) Mechanisms to Ensure Independent Views

          The Company ensures independent views and input are available to the Board via the following
          mechanisms:


          1.   the Board composition and the independence of the independent non-executive Directors shall be
               reviewed by the Nomination Committee on an annual basis;


          2.   the Company has received from each of the independent non-executive Directors a written
               confirmation of his/her independence to the Company. The Company considers all such
               independent non-executive Directors to be independent;

          3.   in view of good corporate governance practices and to avoid conflict of interests, the Directors who
               are also directors and/or senior management of the Company’s controlling shareholders and/or
               certain subsidiaries of the controlling shareholders shall abstain from voting on the relevant Board
               resolutions in relation to the transactions with the controlling shareholders and/or their associates;


          4.   the chairman of the Board shall meet with the independent non-executive Directors at least once
               annually; and


          5.   all members of the Board can seek independent professional advice when necessary in accordance
               with the Company’s policy in order to perform their responsibilities.


          The Board reviews the relevant mechanism on an annual basis to ensure that independent views and
          input are available to the Board, whether in terms of the proportion, recruitment and independence
          of independent non-executive Directors, and to ensure their contribution and access to external
          independent professional advice.

 (V) Board Diversity Policy

    The Company has adopted a Board diversity policy (the “Diversity Policy”), which sets out the approach
    for achieving diversity of the members of the Board. The Company believes that diversity of the members
    of the Board can significantly enhance the quality of the Company’s performance.


    Pursuant to the Diversity Policy, the Company seeks to achieve diversity of the members of the Board
    by considering a number of aspects, including but not limited to gender, race, language, cultural
    background, educational background, industry experience and professional experience.


    In identifying and selecting suitable candidates to serve as a Director of the Company, the Nomination
    Committee shall, before making recommendations to the Board, refer to the above necessary criteria for
    the purpose of executing the corporate strategy and achieving diversity of the members of the Board (where
    appropriate).


    The composition of the members of the Board reflects different cultural and educational backgrounds,
    professional development, length of service, knowledge of the Company, and a broad range of
    individual attributes, interests and values. The Board considers that the current composition of its
    members provides the Company with a balanced and diverse set of skills and experience appropriate
    to the Company’s business. The Board will, taking into consideration the specific needs of the Group’s
    business, continue to review the composition of its members from time to time.


    As at the date of this report, the Board has two female Directors, representing 25% of the members of
    the Board. The Board strives to maintain at least one female Director. When appointing new Directors,
    the Board will fully consider the existing gender ratio in identifying suitable candidates and will strive to
    increase the proportion of female members of the Board.


    The Nomination Committee will review the implementation of the Board Diversity Policy at least annually,
    and will make recommendations on any proposed changes to the Board for the Board’s review and
    approval to ensure its continued appropriateness and effectiveness. During the year, the Board and the
    Nomination Committee have reviewed the implementation and effectiveness of the Board Diversity Policy
    and consider that the Board Diversity Policy and its implementation are sufficient and effective.


    In order to recruit potential successors to the Board to achieve diversity of the members of the Board,
    including gender diversity, the Board has prepared a list setting out the desirable skills, experience,
    qualifications, gender or perspectives that the candidates should possess. If the Board determines that
    an additional or replacement Director is required, it will deploy multiple channels to identify suitable
    Director candidates, including referrals from Directors, Shareholders, management, the Company’s
    advisers and external executive search firms.

      (VI) Workforce Diversity

          For the year ended 31 December 2025, the gender ratio (male to female) in the workforce (including
          senior management) of the Company is approximately 7:1, representing a relatively high proportion of
          female participation within the mining industry. Although the nature of the Group’s business requires
          high physical strength, resulting in the majority of male employees, the Group is committed to achieving
          the goal of employee diversity to the greatest extent and takes gender diversity into consideration when
          recruiting employees. The Company will continue to take measures to promote gender diversity at all
          levels of the Company, including but not limited to the levels of the Board and senior management, and
          to establish channels for female senior managers and potential successors to enter the Board.


      (VII) Remuneration Policy of Directors

          To ensure the ability to attract and retain talents, the Group’s remuneration policy of Directors is
          built upon the principle of providing equitable and market-competitive remuneration packages that
          supports the performance culture and enables the achievement of strategic business goals. The
          Group’s remuneration policy of Directors is, therefore, aimed at providing competitive but not excessive
          remuneration packages to the Directors.


          The Directors’ remuneration comprises fixed salary or service fee and variable components (such as
          bonus), which is benchmarked against companies of comparable business or scale with reference to
          a mix of factors such as the prevailing market conditions, the performance of the Company, and the
          qualifications, skills, experience and educational background of the Directors.


          The Directors’ remuneration is subject to Shareholders’ approval.

               control systems at least annually, and the Company considers that such systems are effective and
               adequate.

    2.   Risk Management and Internal Control Systems

         The risk management and internal control systems have been designed to provide reasonable
         assurance for the legal and compliant operation and management, the safety of assets, the
         truthfulness and completeness of financial reports and related information, to enhance operational
         efficiency and effectiveness, and to facilitate the achievement of the development strategy.


         The Board’s annual review has ensured the adequacy of the resources, staff qualifications and
         experience, training programmes and budget of the Company’s accounting, internal audit and
         financial reporting functions.


         The Board has overall responsibility for maintaining sound and effective risk management (including
         environmental, social and governance risks) and internal control systems throughout the Group,
         which include a defined management structure with limits of authority, and are designed to ensure
         the proper application of accounting standards and the provision of reliable financial data for internal
         use and for publication, as well as to secure compliance with the relevant laws and regulations.
         The systems are developed to provide reasonable, but not absolute, assurance against material
         misstatement or omission, and to manage, but not fully eliminate, the risks of operational systems
         failure and the risks of the Group’s failure in meeting the standards. The Board will review the risk
         management (including environmental, social and governance risks) and internal control systems on
         an ongoing basis.


         The Audit Committee assists the Board in leading the management and overseeing the design,
         implementation and monitoring of the risk management and internal control systems. The Board
         authorized the Audit Committee to supervise the financial reporting system, the risk management
         (including environmental, social and governance risks) and internal control systems of the Company;
         to review the financial controls of the Company and to review the risk management (including
         environmental, social and governance risks) and internal control systems of the Company on an
         annual basis; to discuss the risk management and internal control systems with the management
         and to ensure that the management has performed its duties in establishing effective systems; and
         to consider major investigation findings on risk management and internal control matters and the
         management’s response to such investigation findings on its own initiative or as delegated by the
         Board. The management has reported and confirmed to the Board and the Audit Committee on the
         effectiveness of the risk management and internal control systems.


         The Company’s procedures for identifying, evaluating and managing major risks include but are
         not limited to: 1. identifying, analysing and scientifically predicting possible risks, focusing on key
         and difficult issues such as gold prices, production safety and resource reserves, and formulating
         practical and feasible response plans; 2. in accordance with the principles of concentration
         and classification, reviewing the implementation and management of the major and important
         risk responses of subordinate enterprises at the end of each quarter against the position at the
         beginning of the year, and strengthening risk control; 3. combining comprehensive risk management
         and special risk management, strengthening risk management of major business matters, and
         conducting special risk assessments on significant investments and major mergers and acquisitions;
         4. using internal audit as an important means of risk prevention and control, and completing audit
         projects such as overseas audit, economic responsibility, large fund use and safety special audit,
         with financial audit, engineering audit, mining project acceptance and settlement and other special
         audits as the focus.
134   SHANDONG GOLD MINING CO., LTD.


 SECTION 4 CORPORATE GOVERNANCE, ENVIRONMENT AND SOCIETY

               The Company continues to improve the construction of comprehensive risk management and
               internal control systems, clarifying the risk management and internal control responsibilities of
               the Board, the management, the various departments and the various positions, so as to form a
               comprehensive, all-staff, whole-process, complete-system, and full-coverage risk management and
               internal control mechanism, providing a solid guarantee for the sustainable development of the
               Company.


               The Company’s procedures for examining the effectiveness of the risk management and internal
               control systems include: formulating an evaluation work plan, establishing an evaluation working
               group, conducting on-site testing, identifying control deficiencies, summarising evaluation results,
               and forming an evaluation report. The Board has, in accordance with the requirements for the
               identification of major deficiencies, important deficiencies and general deficiencies under the
               corporate internal control standard system, and having regard to factors such as the Company’s
               scale, industry characteristics, risk preference and risk tolerance, studied and determined the
               specific identification standards of internal control deficiencies applicable to the Company. The
               Company will, in respect of any deficiencies identified, promptly adopt response strategies to
               effectively control risks within tolerable limits.

          3.   Review of the Effectiveness of Risk Management and Internal Control

               For the year ended 31 December 2025, the Board has, through the Audit Committee, conducted an

      (XV) Taxation

          1.   Withholding and Payment of Enterprise Income Tax for Non-resident Enterprise
               Shareholders Outside the PRC

               According to the Enterprise Income Tax Law of the People’s Republic of China and its
               implementation regulations (the “EIT Law”), the tax rate of enterprise income tax applicable to the
               income of a non-resident enterprise deriving from the PRC is 10%. For this purpose, any H Shares
               registered under the name of a non-individual enterprise, including those registered under the name
               of HKSCC Nominees Limited, other nominees or trustees, or other organizations or entities, shall
               be deemed as Shares held by non-resident enterprise shareholders (as defined under the EIT Law),
               and the Company will distribute dividends to such non-resident enterprise shareholders subject to a
               deduction of 10% enterprise income tax withheld and paid by the Company on their behalf.
                                                                                        Annual Report 2025   135


SECTION 4 CORPORATE GOVERNANCE, ENVIRONMENT AND SOCIETY

         Any resident enterprise (as defined under the EIT Law) which has been legally incorporated in
         the PRC, or which was established pursuant to the laws of foreign countries (regions) but has
         its effective place of management in the PRC, and whose name appears on the H Shareholders’
         register of the Company, shall, if it does not wish to have the 10% enterprise income tax withheld
         and paid on its behalf by the Company, deliver in due course to the H share registrar of the
         Company, Tricor Investor Services Limited, a legal opinion ascertaining its status as a resident
         enterprise issued by a qualified PRC lawyer (with the official chop of the law firm issuing the opinion
         affixed thereon) and the relevant documents.


         Pursuant to the “Notice on the Issues Concerning the Administration of Individual Income Tax
         Collection after the Annulment of Document Guo Shui Fa [1993] No. 045” (the “Notice”) issued by
         the State Administration of Taxation on 28 June 2011, the dividend to be distributed by a PRC non-
         foreign-invested enterprise that has issued shares in Hong Kong to overseas resident individual
         shareholders is, in general, subject to individual income tax at a rate of 10%. However, the tax rates
         for respective overseas resident individual shareholders may vary depending on the relevant tax
         agreements between their countries of residence and Mainland China. Accordingly, when distributing
         dividends to individual H Shareholders whose names appear on the H Shareholders’ register of the
         Company on the record date, the Company will withhold 10% of the dividends as individual income
         tax, unless otherwise stipulated in the relevant taxation regulations, tax treaties or the Notice.


         The Company shall not be liable for any claim arising from any delay in, or inaccurate determination
         of, the status of the Shareholders or any disputes over the mechanism of withholding.

    2.   Profit Distribution to Investors of Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect (Shanghai
         Connect)

         For investors of the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (including enterprises and individuals) investing
         in the A Shares listed on the SSE (the “Shanghai Connect”), their dividends will be distributed in
         RMB by the Company through the Shanghai Branch of China Securities Depository and Clearing
         Corporation Limited to the account of the nominee holding such Shares. The Company will withhold
         and pay income tax at the rate of 10% on behalf of those investors, and will report the withholding
         to the competent tax authorities. For investors of Shanghai Connect who are tax residents of other
         countries and whose country of residence has entered into a tax treaty with the PRC stipulating
         a dividend tax rate of lower than 10%, those enterprises and individuals may, on their own or by
         entrusting a withholding agent, apply to the competent tax authorities for the entitlement to the
         relevant rate under such tax treaty. Upon approval by the competent tax authorities, the difference
         between the tax already withheld and the tax payable based on the rate stipulated under such tax
         treaty will be refunded.


         The arrangements regarding the record date and date of distribution of cash dividends and other
         matters for investors of Shanghai Connect will be the same as those for the A Shareholders.
136   SHANDONG GOLD MINING CO., LTD.


 SECTION 4 CORPORATE GOVERNANCE, ENVIRONMENT AND SOCIETY

          3.   Profit Distribution to Investors of Hong Kong Stock Connect (Southbound
               Trading)

               For investors of the SSE and the Shenzhen Stock Exchange (including enterprises and individuals)
               investing in the H Shares listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (the “Southbound Trading”), the
               cash dividends will be distributed in RMB. The arrangements regarding the record date and date
               of distribution of cash dividends and other matters for investors of Southbound Trading will be the
               same as those for the H Shareholders. The relevant taxation policies are governed by the relevant
               provisions of the “Notice on the Tax Policies Related to the Pilot Programme of the Shanghai-
               Hong Kong Stock Connect (Caishui [2014] No. 81)” and the “Notice on the Tax Policies Related
               to the Pilot Programme of the Shenzhen-Hong Kong Stock Connect (Caishui [2016] No. 127)”. For
               dividends received by domestic individual investors from investing in the H Shares listed on the
               Hong Kong Stock Exchange through the Shanghai-Hong Kong Stock Connect and the Shenzhen-
               Hong Kong Stock Connect, the Company will withhold and pay individual income tax at the rate
               of 20% on behalf of the investors. For dividends received by domestic securities investment funds
               from investing in the H Shares listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange through the Shanghai-
               Hong Kong Stock Connect and the Shenzhen-Hong Kong Stock Connect, the tax payable shall be
               the same as that for individual investors. The Company will not withhold or pay the income tax on
               dividends for domestic enterprise investors, and the tax payable shall be reported and paid by such
               enterprise investors themselves.


               Shareholders are recommended to consult their tax advisers regarding the tax implications in the
               PRC, Hong Kong and other countries (regions) of holding and disposing of the Shares.

                                                      internal yields of the non-active enterprises not lower than 8%. The Company will steadily promote the
                                                      resolution of horizontal competition by giving priority to the injection of the aforesaid assets related

                                                      Shandong Gold to sell them to unrelated third parties if the aforesaid relevant conditions for injection

                 Other explanations
                 √ Applicable           □ N/A


                 In order to further advance the international layout of the Company in the capital market, further enhance
                 the capital strength of the Company, optimize its capital structure, promote healthier, more sustainable
                 and high-quality development of the enterprise, and assist in building a globally competitive world-
                 class gold mining enterprise, on 2 September 2025 (before the trading hours of the Hong Kong Stock
                 Exchange), the Company entered into a placing agreement with the placing agents (namely, China
                 International Capital Corporation Hong Kong Securities Limited and CLSA Limited). Pursuant to which,
                 the placing agents agreed to procure, on a best efforts basis, placees to subscribe for the new H Shares
                 (i.e. the overseas listed foreign shares of the Company with a par value of RMB1.00 each in the ordinary
                 share capital of the Company) to be issued by the Company.


                 On 9 September 2025, all the conditions set out in the placing agreement were satisfied, and the placing
                 was completed in accordance with the terms and conditions of the placing agreement. The Company
                 allotted and issued an aggregate of 136,500,000 H placing Shares, with an aggregate nominal value
                 of the H Shares issued of RMB136,500,000. The placing price per placing Share was HK$28.58. The
                 closing price of the H Shares quoted on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange on 1 September 2025 (being
                 the last trading day on which the terms of the placing were determined) was HK$31.40 per Share.
                                                                                   Annual Report 2025   163


                                          SECTION 5              IMPORTANT MATTERS

    Pursuant to the terms and conditions of the placing agreement, the placing agents have successfully
    placed the above Shares to not less than six placees. To the best of the Directors’ knowledge,
    information and belief, after having made all reasonable enquiries, (i) each of the placees and their
    respective ultimate beneficial owners (where applicable) is an independent third party and is not
    connected with the Company or its connected persons; and (ii) upon completion of the placing, none of
    the placees has become a substantial shareholder of the Company (as defined in the Hong Kong Listing
    Rules).


    The gross proceeds from the placing were approximately HK$3,901.17 million. After deduction of the
    commission for the placing and other related costs and expenses of the placing, the net proceeds from
    the placing were approximately HK$3,892.42 million. On this basis, the net placing price receivable by
    the Company per placing Share was approximately HK$28.52. The net proceeds from the placing are
    intended to be used in their entirety for the repayment of debts of the Company.


    For the year ended 31 December 2025, the Group had utilized approximately HK$3,892.42 million of the
    net proceeds from the placing. As at 31 December 2025, the unutilized net proceeds from the placing
    were nil. The actual use of the proceeds and the subsequent intended use by the Company are in full
    conformity with the plan previously disclosed in the placing announcement of the Company dated 2
    September 2025, with no material changes or delay.

          2.   Use of idle proceeds to temporarily supplement working capital
               √ Applicable   □ N/A


               On 19 December 2024, the Company held the 69th meeting of the sixth session of the Board of
               Directors and the 42nd meeting of the sixth session of the Supervisory Committee, at which the
               Proposal on Using Idle Proceeds to Temporarily Supplement Working Capital was considered
               and approved. It was approved that the Company use idle proceeds of RMB550,000,000.00
               to temporarily supplement working capital, with a term not exceeding 12 months, and that the
               Company should timely and fully return such proceeds to the special account for raised funds
               before the expiry of the term. On 17 November 2025, the Company returned the said proceeds
               of RMB550,000,000.00, which had been used to temporarily supplement working capital, to
               the special account for raised funds ahead of schedule, and notified the sponsor and sponsor
               representatives of the Company of such return.


               On 8 December 2025, the Company held the seventh meeting of the seventh session of the Board
               of Directors, at which the Proposal on Using Idle Proceeds to Temporarily Supplement Working
               Capital was considered and approved. It was approved that the Company use idle proceeds of
               RMB500,000,000.00 to temporarily supplement working capital, with a term not exceeding 12
               months, and that the Company should timely and fully return such proceeds to the special account
               for raised funds before the expiry of the term. The Company shall use such proceeds solely for
               production and operation activities related to its principal business.

                                        SECTION 5              IMPORTANT MATTERS

4.   Others
     √ Applicable   □ N/A


     1.   Dongfeng mining area (Dongfeng Phase II Construction Project): Affected by two gold mine
          safety accidents in Shandong Province in early 2021, the Dongfeng mining area of Linglong
          Gold Mine suspended production from the end of January to the end of March 2021 for
          safety inspections; and some areas of the Dongfeng mining area involved Shandong Province
          Ecological Protection Red Line Plan (2016-2020), due to the policy impact of ecological
          protection red line delineation in Shandong Province, the mining license in Dongfeng mining
          area expired on 10 November 2021, and was not renewed, resulting in the suspension of
          production.After the Ecological Protection Red Line Plan was approved, Dongfeng mining area
          obtained the extended mining license in December 2022 and resumed production in January
          2023. During the above suspension period, the construction of the Dongfeng mining area
          project cannot be carried out, so the proceeds have not been fully used. As of the disclosure
          date of this report, production and infrastructure construction have been carried out normally
          within the scope of the mining rights of the Dongfeng mining area, and the part outside the
          scope of mining rights can only be continued after the completion of the boundary expansion
          of mining rights. In July 2025, the plan for the optimization and integration of nature reserves
          and stratified mining has been submitted to the Ministry of Natural Resources. Upon approval,
          Linglong Gold Mine will actively advance the deep boundary expansion and capacity expansion
          of the Dongfeng Mining Area.


     2.   Penglai Mining (The Chugezhuang and Huluxian Mine Construction Projects of Penglai Gold
          Mine): It’s Qijiagou mining area mining rights, Huluxian Gold Mine Area mining rights, Qijiagou-
          Huluxian mining area deep and surrounding gold mine exploration mining rights involve part
          of the Shandong Province Ecological Protection Red Line Plan (2016-2020), due to the policy
          impact of ecological protection red line delineation in Shandong Province, the Chugezhuang
          and Huluxian Gold Mine Area’s boundary and capacity expansion project failed to obtain a
          mining license and carry out project construction. According to the Approval of Shandong
          Provincial People’s Government on the Mineral Resource Integration Plan of GoldMines
          Across 8 Districts (Cities) in Yantai City (《山東省人民政府關於煙台8個區(市)金礦礦產資源整合
          方案的批覆》) (Lu Zheng Zi [2021] No.133) and theOptimised and Adjusted Mineral Resource
          Integration Plan of Gold Mines in Penglai District of Yantai City (《煙台市蓬萊區金礦礦產資
          源整合優化調整方案》) approved by the government of Penglai District, Penglai Mining’s
          Chugezhuang and Huluxian Gold Mine Area’s boundary and capacity expansion project was
          expanded to the“Yanshan Integrated Area Mining Area”. Penglai Mining acquired two mining
          rights owned by Shandong Jinchuang Co., Ltd. and three mining rights owned by Shandong
          Gold Jinchuang Group Co., Ltd., and integrated all the existing mining rights of Penglai Mining
          into one mining right. The construction of the mining area project can only be carried out after
          obtaining a new mining license and project construction procedures. Affected by the above
          factors, the proceeds from the Penglai mining area have not yet been used. Penglai Mining
          has obtained the mining license for Yanshan Integrated Area Mining Area of Shandong Gold
          Group Penglai Mining Co., Ltd. in July 2024. As of the disclosure date of this report, the land
          use pre‑examination submission materials have been approved by the Yantai Municipal Bureau
          of Natural Resources and Planning. Meanwhile, the project approval process is underway, and
          relevant project construction work will be commenced as soon as possible upon completion of
          the approval.

      1.   Financial Services Framework Agreement

           On 28 March 2022, the Company entered into a new financial services framework agreement with SDG
           Finance Co. (the “Financial Services Framework Agreement”), pursuant to which SDG Finance Co.
           will provide the Company and/or our associates with financial services, among others, (i) deposits and
           related services (the “Deposit Services”); (ii) loans, overdrafts, bills and other financing related services
           under the total credit facilities (the “Financing Services”); and (iii) other financial services, including
           settlement, guarantee, insurance agent and financial consultancy (the “Other Financial Services”), for
           a term from 31 May 2022 to 31 December 2024, in order to facilitate the Group’s operational needs of
           financial services.
